# `silk/crypto/ml_kem`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Agree on a shared secret with ML-KEM (FIPS 203), the module-lattice key encapsulation
mechanism, at the levels ML-KEM-512, ML-KEM-768, and ML-KEM-1024.

## When to use
Use [`MlKem`](#MlKem) when a shared secret must stay secret also against an attacker with a large
quantum computer, for example in a hybrid TLS 1.3 group such as `X25519MLKEM768`. One side makes
a key pair with [`MlKem.keyPairFromSeed`](#MlKem.impl.keyPairFromSeed) and sends the encapsulation key. The other side calls
[`MlKem.encapsulate`](#MlKem.impl.encapsulate), keeps the 32-byte shared secret, and sends the ciphertext back. The first
side gets the same secret with [`MlKem.decapsulate`](#MlKem.impl.decapsulate). Use `silk.crypto.ml_key` to read and write
the keys in PKCS #8 and SubjectPublicKeyInfo.

## Details
The caller gives every buffer, so nothing allocates. A key pair comes from a 64-byte seed
`d || z`, the form that PKCS #8 stores; the functions of [`MlKemParameters`](#MlKemParameters) give the sizes.
Decapsulation runs in constant time for the secret values and returns the implicit-rejection
secret for a ciphertext that does not match, as FIPS 203 says, so it never fails for a
ciphertext of the right length. The NTT uses 16-bit Montgomery products with lazy reduction.
The encapsulation and decapsulation keys are checked as FIPS 203 section 7 asks.

## Errors
- [`MlKemError`](#MlKemError) for a buffer of the wrong length, or for a key that fails the checks of FIPS
  203.

## Gotchas
ML-KEM does not tell you who the other side is; authenticate the exchange, for example with a
signature. Secrets are not erased.

## Examples
### Agree on a secret
```silk
import silk.core.result { Result }
import silk.crypto.ml_kem { MlKem, MlKemError, MlKemParameters }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let parameters = MlKemParameters.MlKem768
  // Real programs fill the seed and the message from a secure `Random` provider.
  let seed: [u8; 64] = [1; 64]
  let mut encapsulationKey: [u8; 1184] = [0; 1184]
  let mut decapsulationKey: [u8; 2400] = [0; 2400]
  match MlKem.keyPairFromSeed(parameters, &seed, &mut encapsulationKey, &mut decapsulationKey) {
    Result<(), MlKemError>.Success { .. } => {}
    Result<(), MlKemError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let message: [u8; 32] = [2; 32]
  let mut ciphertext: [u8; 1088] = [0; 1088]
  let sent = match MlKem.encapsulateWith(parameters, &encapsulationKey, &message, &mut ciphertext) {
    Result<[u8; 32], MlKemError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<[u8; 32], MlKemError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  let received = match MlKem.decapsulate(parameters, &decapsulationKey, &ciphertext) {
    Result<[u8; 32], MlKemError>.Success { value } => value
    Result<[u8; 32], MlKemError>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  if sent[0] != received[0] || sent[31] != received[31] {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `MlKem` with `import silk.crypto.ml_kem { MlKem }`.

<a id="MlKem"></a>

## `MlKem`

```silk
pub struct MlKem
```

The functions of ML-KEM.

### When to use
Make a key pair with [`MlKem.keyPairFromSeed`](#MlKem.impl.keyPairFromSeed), encapsulate with [`MlKem.encapsulate`](#MlKem.impl.encapsulate), and
decapsulate with [`MlKem.decapsulate`](#MlKem.impl.decapsulate).

### Details
Each function takes the parameter set and the caller's buffers, which must have the lengths of
[`MlKemParameters`](#MlKemParameters). The decapsulation key holds the encapsulation key; see
[`MlKem.encapsulationKeyOf`](#MlKem.impl.encapsulationKeyOf).

<a id="MlKem.impl.keyPairFromSeed"></a>

### Associated function `keyPairFromSeed`

```silk
pub fn keyPairFromSeed(
    parameters: MlKemParameters,
    seed: &[u8],
    encapsulationKey: &mut [u8],
    decapsulationKey: &mut [u8],
  ) -> Result<(), MlKemError>
```

Writes the key pair of ML-KEM.KeyGen_internal for the 64-byte `seed`, `d` followed by `z`,
into `encapsulationKey` and `decapsulationKey`.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength` if `seed` is not 64 bytes, or a key buffer does not have the length of the
  parameter set. The buffers do not change.

<a id="MlKem.impl.generateSeed"></a>

### Associated function `generateSeed`

```silk
pub effect fn generateSeed() -> [u8; 64] ? &mut Random
```

Returns a new 64-byte seed from the ambient `Random`, for [`MlKem.keyPairFromSeed`](#MlKem.impl.keyPairFromSeed).

The `Random` provider must be cryptographically secure.

<a id="MlKem.impl.encapsulate"></a>

### Associated function `encapsulate`

```silk
pub effect fn encapsulate(
    parameters: MlKemParameters,
    encapsulationKey: &[u8],
    ciphertext: &mut [u8],
  ) -> Result<[u8; 32], MlKemError> ? &mut Random
```

Writes a ciphertext for `encapsulationKey` into `ciphertext` and returns the 32-byte shared
secret, with a 32-byte message from the ambient `Random`.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength` if `encapsulationKey` or `ciphertext` does not have the length of the
  parameter set.
- `InvalidEncapsulationKey` if the key fails the modulus check.

`ciphertext` does not change on an error.

<a id="MlKem.impl.encapsulateWith"></a>

### Associated function `encapsulateWith`

```silk
pub fn encapsulateWith(
    parameters: MlKemParameters,
    encapsulationKey: &[u8],
    message: &[u8],
    ciphertext: &mut [u8],
  ) -> Result<[u8; 32], MlKemError>
```

Writes the ciphertext of ML-KEM.Encaps_internal for `encapsulationKey` and the 32-byte
`message` into `ciphertext`, and returns the shared secret.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength` for a key, message, or ciphertext buffer of the wrong length.
- `InvalidEncapsulationKey` if the key fails the modulus check.

#### Gotchas
It is for test vectors. A message that is not fresh random bytes breaks the security, so use
[`MlKem.encapsulate`](#MlKem.impl.encapsulate).

<a id="MlKem.impl.decapsulate"></a>

### Associated function `decapsulate`

```silk
pub fn decapsulate(parameters: MlKemParameters, decapsulationKey: &[u8], ciphertext: &[u8]) -> Result<
    [u8; 32],
    MlKemError,
  >
```

Returns the 32-byte shared secret of ML-KEM.Decaps for `ciphertext`.

A ciphertext of the right length that was not made for this key gives the implicit-rejection
secret of FIPS 203, a value that the sender cannot predict, and not an error. The time does
not depend on the secret values or on whether the ciphertext matched.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength` if `decapsulationKey` or `ciphertext` does not have the length of the
  parameter set.
- `InvalidDecapsulationKey` if the key fails the hash check.
